display.title: Vayeitzei: Yaakov's Ladder of Prayer
display.summary_short: Why did the angels in Yaakov's dream go up before coming down? The Zohar explains that the ladder is davening, carrying our prayers up and Hashem's blessings down.
display.summary_long: A parsha talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for Parshas Vayeitzei. Uncle Yossi describes Yaakov Avinu's dream of a ladder standing on the ground and reaching to heaven, with angels going up and down. Why up first, when angels live in heaven? The Zohar of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai answers: the ladder is tefillah. The words we say in davening become angels that climb up to Hashem and repeat our prayers, and Hashem sends His blessings back down the same ladder. Tzaddikim often learn Torah secrets while their souls rise during sleep, and this dream was so important that it is written in the Torah. As the Rambam says, whatever we need, we can turn straight to Hashem. So we should say every word of davening clearly and carefully, so the angel it creates is strong and healthy, and daven with joy, as Dovid HaMelech teaches, because we trust that Hashem hears and answers.
display.lesson: Daven every word clearly and joyfully: your prayers climb up to Hashem, and His blessings come back down to you.
